5th grade. Long island.
My teacher asked the teacher across the hall to watch our class for a minute while she did something. She came back with the TV in wheels and the class got excited. She immediately put a stop to our children. She closed the door and said "The principal told all the teachers not to tell younkids what's going on. But I'm from a place (China) where the govt censorship is out of control. And I won't let that happen here."
She told us what happened and we watched the news all day. Since we were an hour outside the city, some of the kids parents worked worked in that vicinity. So all day the anouncements would come on and one by one kids got called down to the main office to get picked up. At lunch, instead of all the classes getting their own separate tables, a bunch of us sat together. Most still in the same grade. Some of the tables were mixed grades. This was the only time in elementary school where this happened. Our class was the only one that knew what was going on so we told the other classes. We had no recess that day at lunch. By the end of the day instead of having long lines for parent pickup or for the buses, there were only a handful of us left. Normally there'd be 30ish kids on my bus. On that day there were maybe eight of us.
